title: Introduce traffic-conditioned stability sieve for rollout guards
author: Ava Lin
description:
Motivation: Reduce noisy rollback triggers caused by transient traffic composition shifts during canaries. We observed multiple false-positive canary failures when a small cohort of high-latency traffic (e.g., long-context batched requests or heavy re-ranking paths) temporarily increased the metric variance. This PR implements a traffic-conditioned stability sieve that (1) segments traffic by configurable attributes (route, request shape, sequence length bucket, customer tier), (2) computes per-cohort stability scores using an adaptive quantile ensemble, and (3) fuses cohort signals with global detectors to produce a conservative rollout gate.
Design: - Traffic partitioner: lightweight sampling-based partitioning upstream of the canary evaluator.
- Cohort detectors: run percentile- and bootstrap-based checks per cohort to detect sustained degradation.
- Sieve fusion: weights cohort alerts by statistical significance and traffic volume; small noisy cohorts are downweighted to avoid overreaction.
- Backfill & warmup: the sieve warms with a short sampling window (configurable) and supports backfill from historical telemetry to avoid cold-start false alarms.
- Operator controls: new rollout policy knobs (min_cohort_coverage, significance_threshold, warmup_minutes) exposed in canary configs and Redwood Console.
Implementation scope: - Core evaluator: src/canary/stability_sieve.py
- Partitioning helpers: src/canary/partition.py
- E2E tests & unit tests: tests/canary/test_stability_sieve.py, tests/e2e/canary_traffic_flow.py
- Dashboards: dashboards/perf/canary-stability.jsonnet
- Alerting rules: alerting/rules/canary-sieve-alerts.yaml
- Docs: docs/design/traffic_conditioned_sieve.md
Migration & deployment notes: - Default rollout policy unchanged; sieve is opt-in via canary policy flag staged=true.
- We will enable in internal canary clusters for 72h and monitor false-positive/false-negative rates before flipping to opt-out.
Checklist: - [x] Partitioning + detector implementation
- [x] Unit tests with synthetic traffic mixes
- [x] E2E test with canary harness
- [x] Dashboard & runbook entries
- [x] Backwards-compatible config
- [x] Performance microbench (adds ~2.3ms eval overhead at 50k rps with sharded sampling)

review_comments: Mateo Cruz: Nice approach; two questions: how do we guard against cohort explosion (many tiny cohorts) and what's the maintenance burden for the dashboard filters?

Ava Lin: We cap cohort cardinality via sampling and a top-k retention policy; tiny cohorts (<0.5% traffic) are aggregated into an 'other' bucket by default. Dashboard filters are templated and auto-populated from partition keys to minimize manual upkeep.
Priya Singh: Unit tests look good. Can we add a small regression test that simulates a heavy re-ranking workload to validate downweighting?
Ava Lin: Added an e2e scenario in tests/e2e/canary_traffic_flow.py that includes a heavy re-ranker cohort and asserts no immediate rollback when global traffic remains stable.
Jonah Becker: Performance microbench numbers OK but please document CPU/memory profile for the new sampler under peak load.
Ava Lin: Included a short microbench in docs/design and added perf notes in the PR body. Sampler uses reservoir sampling and keeps ~1k cohort keys in-memory per evaluator shard (~8MB).

release_notes: Add traffic-conditioned stability sieve: opt-in canary rollout guard that reduces false-positive rollbacks by fusing per-cohort stability signals with global detectors. Configurable partitioning and warmup; opt-in for 72h internal evaluation before broader rollout.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature flag canary.sieve.staged=true in internal canary clusters. Monitor metric: canary.false_positive_rate and canary.sieve.coverage for first 72h. If coverage < 40% or false_positive_rate increases, flip back and open ENG-7899.
deployment_plan: Stage deploy to internal-canary -> monitor 72h -> enable on canary-stage -> 1-week canary window -> opt-in for open beta. Rollback path: set canary.sieve.staged=false and revert via feature-flag disabling.
testing_summary: Unit tests: deterministic synthetic mixes cover percentile and bootstrap detectors. E2E: full canary harness with traffic shaping; regression test for heavy re-ranker cohort added. Microbench: 50k rps slice shows ~2.3ms evaluator overhead; memory footprint ~8MB/shard.
